title: Choking — hit the back, then pull the belly
applies_to: Someone with food or an object blocking their throat, who cannot cough, speak, or breathe.

citations.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Basic Life Support
citations.section: Foreign body airway obstruction in adults

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC 2020

steps.text: Ask them: are you choking? If they can cough, speak, or breathe, tell them to keep coughing and stay with them.
If they cannot cough, speak, or breathe, shout for help and get someone to call for an ambulance now.
Stand to the side and slightly behind them. Hold their chest with one hand and lean them forward so the object can come out of the mouth.
Hit them firmly between the shoulder blades with the heel of your other hand. Do this up to 5 times.
Look after each hit. Stop as soon as the object comes out or they start breathing.
If the hits did not work, stand behind them and put both arms around their middle. Make a fist and place it just above the belly button.
Hold your fist with your other hand and pull sharply inwards and upwards. Do this up to 5 times.
Keep going: 5 hits on the back, then 5 pulls on the belly, until the object comes out or help arrives.

do_not: Do not put your fingers into their mouth to feel for the object. You can push it further down.
Do not slap them on the back while they are sitting upright and coughing well. A good cough shifts more than you can.
Do not pull on the belly of a baby under 1 year old. Support them face down along your arm and hit the back instead.
Do not pull on the belly of a pregnant person, or of someone too large for you to reach around. Pull on the lower chest instead.
escalate_if: They stop answering you — lower them to the floor, call for help, and start pushing on the chest.
The object comes out but they still cannot breathe well — keep them sitting up and get them to hospital.
You pulled on their belly and it worked — they still need to be checked at a hospital, because the pull can hurt the inside.
